## 🔹 1. Multi-Company HR & Payroll System


**Konsep:**
Satu platform HR untuk banyak perusahaan.

**Fitur utama:**
- Multi-company login (company A gak bisa lihat data B)
- Employee management (CRUD karyawan)
- Attendance (check-in/out)
- Payroll (gaji, bonus, potongan)
- Role-based access (HR, manager, employee)

**Nilai jual:**
- Real-world banget (dipakai banyak startup)
- Kompleksitas medium–high → bagus buat CV

---

## 🔹 2. Multi-Company URL Shortener (Upgrade dari project kamu)


**Konsep:**
Kembangkan project shortener kamu jadi SaaS multi-tenant.

**Tambahan fitur:**
- Tiap company punya:
  - domain sendiri (misal: `go.companyA.com`)
  - analytics terpisah
- Team collaboration (shared links)
- API key per company
- Billing (basic vs premium)

**Nilai jual:**
- Upgrade langsung dari project kamu → sangat kuat di CV
- Bisa nunjukin skill backend + system design

---

## 🔹 3. Multi-Company Project Management Tool (Mini Jira)


**Konsep:**
Tool kayak Jira tapi versi sederhana.

**Fitur:**
- Workspace per company
- Project & task (kanban board)
- Assign user
- Deadline & status tracking
- Comment & activity log

**Nilai jual:**
- Banyak recruiter suka lihat ini
- Cocok buat fullstack

---

## 🔹 4. Multi-Company E-Commerce Admin (Headless Backend)


**Konsep:**
Satu backend untuk banyak toko online.

**Fitur:**
- Product & inventory per company
- Order management
- Payment integration (Midtrans cocok banget sama project kamu)
- Analytics penjualan

**Nilai jual:**
- Kuat di backend + integrasi payment
- Bisa dikaitkan dengan pengalaman kamu sebelumnya

---

## 🔹 5. Multi-Company API Key & Usage Dashboard (Developer SaaS)


**Konsep:**
Platform untuk developer manage API mereka.

**Fitur:**
- Generate API key per company
- Rate limiting
- Usage tracking (requests/day)
- Billing berdasarkan usage

**Nilai jual:**
- Lebih advanced (mirip Stripe / OpenAI dashboard)
- Cocok kalau kamu mau keliatan “high-level engineer”

---

## 🔥 Rekomendasi (Berdasarkan kamu)
Dari semua ini, yang paling cocok buat kamu:

👉 **Multi-Company URL Shortener SaaS**

Kenapa:
- Kamu **sudah punya base project**
- Tinggal evolve ke:
  - multi-tenant architecture
  - analytics advanced
  - Redis (yang tadi kamu tanya bisa kepake banget di sini)

  - shared DB + tenant_id

# 🧠 Konsep Inti Multi-Company



Bayangin kamu bikin satu aplikasi:

- Company A daftar → punya user, data sendiri  
- Company B daftar → juga punya user, data sendiri  
- Tapi… **mereka pakai aplikasi yang sama**

👉 Nah itu disebut **multi-tenant**

---

# 🔑 Komponen Penting

## 1. Tenant (Company)
- Setiap perusahaan = **1 tenant**
- Biasanya punya:
  - `id`
  - `name`
  - `subscription_plan`

Contoh:
```json
Company A → tenant_id = 1
Company B → tenant_id = 2
```

---

## 2. User & Role
- User selalu “milik” company tertentu

Contoh:
```json
User:
- id: 10
- email: a@companyA.com
- tenant_id: 1
- role: admin
```

👉 Artinya:
- User A **tidak boleh akses** data tenant lain

---

## 3. Tenant Identification (Cara Bedain Company)

Ada 3 cara umum:

### 🔹 a. Subdomain (paling keren)
```
companyA.app.com
companyB.app.com
```

### 🔹 b. Path
```
app.com/companyA
```

### 🔹 c. Dari user login
- Sistem baca `tenant_id` dari user

---

## 4. Database Design (INI PALING KRUSIAL)

Ada 3 pendekatan:

---

### 🟢 1. Shared Database, Shared Tables (paling umum)


Semua data di satu tabel, pakai `tenant_id`.

Contoh:
```sql
Table: links

id | short_url | tenant_id
1  | abc123    | 1
2  | xyz789    | 2
```

👉 Query harus selalu:
```sql
SELECT * FROM links WHERE tenant_id = 1;
```

✅ Pro:
- Simple
- Murah
- Cepat develop

❌ Cons:
- Risk kalau lupa filter → data bocor

---

### 🟡 2. Shared DB, Separate Schema
- 1 database, tapi tiap company punya schema sendiri

```
companyA.users
companyB.users
```

✅ Lebih aman  
❌ Lebih kompleks

---

### 🔴 3. Separate Database per Company
- Tiap company punya DB sendiri

✅ Isolasi terbaik  
❌ Mahal & ribet scaling

---

# 🔐 5. Data Isolation (WAJIB BANGET)

Ini inti dari multicompany:

👉 **Tidak boleh ada data leakage**

Contoh bug fatal:
```sql
SELECT * FROM links;
```

Harusnya:
```sql
SELECT * FROM links WHERE tenant_id = current_user.tenant_id;
```

---

# ⚙️ Flow Sederhana

## Saat user login:
1. User login
2. Sistem ambil:
   - `user_id`
   - `tenant_id`
3. Simpan di session / JWT

---

## Saat request:
1. User request (misal: lihat link)
2. Backend:
   - baca `tenant_id`
   - filter data

---

# 🧱 Contoh Nyata (Relate ke Project Kamu)

Kalau kamu bikin **URL Shortener Multi-Company**:

### Tanpa multicompany:
- Semua user lihat semua link ❌

### Dengan multicompany:
- Company A:
  - link: `abc.com/a1`
- Company B:
  - link: `xyz.com/b1`

👉 Mereka **tidak bisa lihat data satu sama lain**

---

# 🚀 Insight Penting (Level Lebih Dalam)

Kalau kamu mau keliatan “pro”:

### 1. Middleware Tenant Filter
- Jangan manual di tiap query
- Buat middleware otomatis inject `tenant_id`

---

### 2. Row-Level Security (Advanced)
Kalau pakai PostgreSQL:

- Bisa enforce langsung di DB
- Lebih aman dari human error

---

### 3. Scaling Strategy
- Mulai dari:
  - shared DB
- Kalau besar:
  - migrate ke separate DB

---

Multi-company =  
👉 **1 aplikasi, banyak perusahaan, data terisolasi**

Kunci utamanya:
- `tenant_id`
- data isolation
- auth + role
- database design

# 💻 Contoh Implementasi (Node.js Express)

```javascript
    tenant_id: 1
  };
  next();
}
```

---

```javascript
app.get("/notes", authMiddleware, async (req, res) => {
  const notes = await db.query(
    "SELECT * FROM notes WHERE tenant_id = ?",
    [req.user.tenant_id]
  );

  res.json(notes);
});
```

---

## Create Note
```javascript
app.post("/notes", authMiddleware, async (req, res) => {
  const { title, content } = req.body;

  await db.query(
    "INSERT INTO notes (title, content, tenant_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
    [title, content, req.user.tenant_id]
  );

  res.send("Created");
});
```

**Chat_message Title: **

You are a senior fullstack engineer. Help me build a multi-tenant marketplace e-commerce web application from scratch.

## Project Overview
I want to build a multi-company (multi-tenant) e-commerce platform focused on shoes. Multiple brands (e.g., Nike, Adidas, New Balance) can register as sellers and manage their own products. Customers can browse products from different sellers and purchase them in a single checkout.

## Core Requirements
1. Multi-tenant system:
   - Each company (seller) is a tenant
   - Data must be isolated using tenant_id
   - Sellers can only access their own data

2. User roles:
   - Buyer
   - Seller (belongs to a company)
   - Admin

3. Features:
   - Authentication (JWT-based)
   - Seller dashboard:
     - Create, update, delete products
     - View orders (only their own)
   - Buyer features:
     - Browse products
     - Add to cart (multi-seller)
     - Checkout

4. Order system:
   - A single checkout may include products from multiple sellers
   - The system must split orders per seller (tenant_id)
   - Each seller sees only their own orders

5. Database design:
   - Design normalized relational schema
   - Must include:
     - users
     - companies (tenants)
     - products
     - carts
     - orders
     - order_items
   - Use tenant_id for isolation

6. Tech Stack:
   - Backend: Node.js (Express)
   - Database: PostgreSQL
   - ORM: Prisma (preferred)
   - Frontend: Next.js (App Router)
   - Auth: JWT
   - Optional: Redis for caching

7. Deliverables:
   - Step-by-step implementation plan
   - Folder structure (backend + frontend)
   - Database schema (Prisma)
   - API design (REST)
   - Basic UI pages (Next.js)
   - Example code for critical parts:
     - Auth middleware
     - Tenant isolation
     - Order splitting logic

8. Important:
   - Focus on clean architecture and scalability
   - Explain each step clearly
   - Do not skip foundational setup

Start by:
1. Designing the database schema (Prisma)
2. Then backend structure
3. Then core API endpoints
4. Then frontend pages

Guide me step-by-step as if I am building a production-ready system.

# 🧱 PRISMA SCHEMA (FINAL)

Ini sudah siap kamu pakai langsung 👇

```prisma
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

//////////////////////////////////////////////////
// ENUMS
//////////////////////////////////////////////////

enum Role {
  BUYER
  SELLER
  ADMIN
}

enum OrderStatus {
  PENDING
  PAID
  SHIPPED
  COMPLETED
  CANCELLED
}

//////////////////////////////////////////////////
// USERS & COMPANIES
//////////////////////////////////////////////////

model User {
  id          String   @id @default(uuid())
  email       String   @unique
  role        Role     @default(BUYER)
  companyId   String?  
  company     Company? @relation(fields: [companyId], references: [id])
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())

  cart        Cart?
  orders      Order[]

  @@map("users")
}

model Company {
  id          String    @id @default(uuid())
  name        String
  description String?
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())

  users       User[]
  products    Product[]
  orders      Order[]

  @@map("companies")
}

//////////////////////////////////////////////////
// PRODUCT DOMAIN
//////////////////////////////////////////////////

model Category {
  id        String    @id @default(uuid())
  name      String
  products  Product[]

  @@map("categories")
}

model Product {
  id          String          @id @default(uuid())
  name        String
  description String?
  price       Int
  imageUrl    String?
  companyId   String
  categoryId  String
  createdAt   DateTime        @default(now())

  company     Company         @relation(fields: [companyId], references: [id])
  category    Category        @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])
  sizes       ProductSize[]
  cartItems   CartItem[]
  orderItems  OrderItem[]

  @@map("products")
}

model ProductSize {
  id         String   @id @default(uuid())
  productId  String
  size       Int
  stock      Int

  product    Product  @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id])

  @@unique([productId, size])
  @@map("product_sizes")
}

//////////////////////////////////////////////////
// CART DOMAIN
//////////////////////////////////////////////////

model Cart {
  id        String      @id @default(uuid())
  userId    String      @unique
  createdAt DateTime    @default(now())

  user      User        @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  items     CartItem[]

  @@map("carts")
}

model CartItem {
  id         String   @id @default(uuid())
  cartId     String
  productId  String
  size       Int
  quantity   Int

  cart       Cart     @relation(fields: [cartId], references: [id])
  product    Product  @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id])

  @@map("cart_items")
}

//////////////////////////////////////////////////
// ORDER DOMAIN (CORE MARKETPLACE)
//////////////////////////////////////////////////

model Order {
  id          String       @id @default(uuid())
  userId      String
  companyId   String
  totalPrice  Int
  status      OrderStatus  @default(PENDING)
  createdAt   DateTime     @default(now())

  user        User         @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  company     Company      @relation(fields: [companyId], references: [id])
  items       OrderItem[]

  @@map("orders")
}

model OrderItem {
  id         String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId    String
  productId  String
  size       Int
  quantity   Int
  price      Int

  order      Order    @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id])
  product    Product  @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id])

  @@map("order_items")
}
```
